content_metadata.description: This video provides an educational overview of the genetic basis of cystic fibrosis, focusing on its association with the CFTR gene located on chromosome 7 and its implications at the cellular level.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the gene associated with cystic fibrosis?
What is the specific location of the CFTR gene on chromosome 7?

qAndA.answer: It shows an animation of chloride ions moving in and out of a healthy cell, implying that CFTR acts as an ion channel.
qAndA.question: How does the video illustrate the function of the CFTR gene?

qAndA.answer: Chloride ion movement is disrupted, leading to the buildup of sticky mucus within the lungs.
qAndA.question: What happens in the cells of individuals with cystic fibrosis?

qAndA.answer: The video is informative and educational, aiming to explain the genetic basis of cystic fibrosis in a clear and visually engaging way.
qAndA.question: What is the overall tone and purpose of the video?

activities.description: Display of a human karyotype (chromosome set).
Showing an illustration of a human lung beside chromosome 7.
Zooming into a section of the lung illustration to show cells.
Animating chloride ions moving in and out of a healthy cell.
Showing a cell with cystic fibrosis and the buildup of mucus.
Highlighting a band on chromosome 7 labeled '7q31.2'.
Illustrating the meaning of '7q31.2' using color-coded bands.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The animation of chloride ions moving in and out of a healthy cell, compared to the cell with cystic fibrosis, helps viewers understand the impact of the genetic mutation on a cellular level.

mood.description: Curious. The visuals and simple animation style create a sense of curiosity and exploration.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of cystic fibrosis as a genetic disorder.
Linking cystic fibrosis to the lungs.
Visualizing the cellular level impact of cystic fibrosis.
Pinpointing the exact location of the CFTR gene on chromosome 7 and explaining the band nomenclature.

youtube_description:
www.sicklecellanaemia.org
Introduction to genetics. This is an animated resource part 6 of 6.

This open educational resource is part of a suite of free teaching materials to raise awareness of sickle cell disease. Sickle cell is a haemoglobin disorder, and these resources help you understand the genetics behind the condition. We hope that students studying medicine and biomedical science will find them useful - and do recommend them to your teachers!

This sickle cell disease project (SCOOTER) was funded by the UK Open Education Programme supporting the sharing of educational materials and expertise in sickle cell disease and other blood disorders. We are proud to be part of the global open education community and passionately believe that learning should be accessible and open to anyone who wishes to participate.
